study_title: ORIGIN: A preregistered multimodal comparison of brain-body models of emotion episodes
primary_question: Do distributed predictive-interoceptive state models predict held-out multichannel emotion-episode observations better than functional-circuit and general-arousal alternatives?

planned_sample.minimum_confirmatory_analysis_set: 150 participants with at least 80% valid trials
planned_sample.stopping_rule: no outcome-contingent expansion after enrollment; under-target data are reported as under-target

manipulations: mild inspiratory resistance versus sham with airway-pressure and respiration verification
primary_outcome: Nested-cross-validated, equally outcome-family-weighted expected log predictive density on held-out participant/context partitions. ORIGIN support requires at least 0.02 nats per trial mean improvement over the null, bootstrap 95% lower confidence bound above zero, and no Brier-score worsening greater than 0.005.
causal_status: The respiratory calibration module experimentally varies a mild bodily input. The primary neural measurements remain observational; any neural perturbation extension is future work requiring a separately approved protocol and explicit causal estimand.
no_claims: No human data have been collected.
No decoding accuracy, effect size, or intervention result is claimed.
